eligibility_reason: Reanalysis/reproducibility check of the same data: the authors re-obtained the same New Jersey Division of Taxation income tax records for 2000-2007 used by Young and Varner (2011), truncated at YV's own May 6, 2008 cutoff 'to match the original data as closely as possible', re-estimated YV's models 1-3, then respecified them (nominal income thresholds, dropping in-migrants, probit); no new sample, population or period is observed.
notes: Title calls it 'A Replication of Millionaire Migration and State Taxation of Top Incomes' (Young, C.; Varner, C., 2011, National Tax Journal 64:255-284). The data were independently requested from the state rather than taken from YV, but they are the same administrative records for the same taxpayers and years ('Like YV, we obtained income tax records from the New Jersey Division of Taxation for 2000 through 2007. To match the original data as closely as possible, we used the authors' reported May 6, 2008, cutoff date'; 'Our estimated coefficients are very similar to YV's, suggesting that there are no important differences between our respective data sets'). Under the codebook this is the 'reanalysis or reproducibility check of the same data' genre, so no entry. If a second coder counts the independently re-acquired records as new data, the single candidate entry would be: YV (2011) claim that the 2004 millionaires' tax had no significant effect on relative net out-migration of >$500k earners (post-2003 x millionaire coefficient ~0.4-0.5 per 1,000, n.s.). The straight reproduction (Table 1, models 1-3: 0.144/0.046 n.s. vs YV 0.479/0.413 n.s.) agrees with YV's null, but the authors' conclusion disputes YV's claim: 'YV's contention that the 2004 tax increase had no effect on relative millionaire out-migration appears to have depended on their questionable inclusion of in-migrants in their sample' (out-migration-only models show significant positive coefficients). Such an entry would most plausibly be coded inconclusive (null reproduced under YV's specification, rejected under the authors' preferred robustness specifications), replication_type direct.
